title: Bird Banter #1: The Kingfisher Debt
style: Hand-painted storybook illustration, rich watercolor and ink on textured paper, warm cinematic light, expressive animals with very human emotions, dry wit, sophisticated and a little melancholic rather than childish, the main subjects kept in the middle of the frame with room above them, {frame}, no text, no letters, no watermark.

story.want: to catch one perfect fish by sunset to keep his father's branch
story.risk: losing the branch and his father's legacy
reversals: Nia only wanted the branch to see her nest
Marco gives away the fish and the river's last rule rewards it
story.open_thread: Whose egg is it, why does it hum, and how was the turtle on both banks?
story.lesson: Giving away the thing you most need, to someone who needs it more, is how you keep what matters.

characters.marco: Marco: a large male common kingfisher with brilliant electric-blue back, orange chest, thick black beak, a slightly ruffled blue crest, proud puffed-out chest and fierce amber eyes.
characters.nia: Nia: a smaller female common kingfisher with brilliant turquoise back, orange chest, black beak with a hint of red at the base, sleek smooth head feathers and sharp determined dark eyes.
characters.turtle: A huge calm old river turtle with a mossy shell, half-closed sleepy eyes and a peaceful expression.
characters.witness: The Witness: a small plump green frog with heavy-lidded eyes and a permanently blank, unimpressed expression, sitting perfectly still on a lily pad.
characters.egg: A single pale speckled egg resting in a small twig nest, with a faint warm glow that seems slightly too bright.
characters.human: Sam: a plain white round-headed stick figure in a grey hoodie and black trousers, thin dark outline, big worried eyes, small scar on the left cheek.
characters.colleague: Jo: a plain white round-headed stick figure in a navy sweater with a lanyard, thin dark outline, tired eyes, messy stack of papers always nearby.
characters.boss: The boss: a tall friendly stick figure with brown hair in a blue shirt and lanyard, thin dark outline, warm smile.

scenes.narration: Marco had until sunset to catch one fish, or lose everything.
scenes.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of Marco perched on a weathered branch above a golden river at low sun, amber eyes locked on the water, chest puffed with fierce resolve. In the soft background the frog sits motionless on a lily pad staring blankly.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same shot a moment later: Marco leans forward, wings half-spread, beak pointed down at the water, ripple beginning below him; the frog has not moved at all.

scenes.narration: The branch was his father's. Three thousand dives, all from this one spot.
scenes.image_prompt: Low angle of the old branch, its bark worn smooth in one spot where talons have gripped it for generations; Marco stands on the worn patch, small against a huge orange sky, a single faded blue feather caught in the bark beside him.

scenes.narration: Across the river, Nia watched. She wanted that branch more.
scenes.image_prompt: Nia perched on a far bank reed staring across the water with intense unblinking dark eyes, wings tucked tight; in the foreground reeds the frog is also staring, at Nia, with total blankness.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same shot: Nia has silently shifted one step closer along the reed, her gaze unchanged; the frog's head has turned exactly the same amount.

scenes.narration: The old turtle, keeper of the river, set the terms.
scenes.image_prompt: The huge old mossy turtle on a flat rock mid-river, eyes half closed, presiding; Marco and Nia stand on either side at a respectful distance, both rigid and anxious, tiny beside the shell.

scenes.narration: One perfect fish. Delivered before the last light. No exceptions.
scenes.delivery: each sentence heavier, final word flat
scenes.image_prompt: Close on the turtle's ancient face, one eye slowly opening, a glowing sunset reflected in it; in the blurred foreground Marco gulps, beak slightly open.

scenes.narration: Marco dived. The river gave him a boot.
scenes.image_prompt: Marco bursting up from the water in a frozen spray of droplets, clutching one enormous waterlogged brown leather boot in his beak, eyes wide with disbelief, river mud on his crest.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same moment: the boot has swung forward, pouring water in an arc over a very unimpressed Marco.

scenes.narration: Third dive. Eleven seconds underwater. Nobody breathed.
scenes.image_prompt: Nia and the frog on the bank staring at a perfectly still, dark river surface with a single ring of ripples, both frozen with identical tension; golden light on the water.

scenes.narration: He surfaced with a trout. Silver. Magnificent. Perfect.
scenes.image_prompt: Marco rocketing out of the water in a glittering crown of droplets, a huge silver speckled trout flashing in his beak, wings blazing blue and orange against the sunset, a rainbow in the spray.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same shot at peak height: Marco banking toward the bank, trout dripping gold, sun flaring behind him.

scenes.narration: Then Nia struck. The trout vanished into the sky.
scenes.image_prompt: Nia a blur of turquoise diving in from the side, snatching the trout out of Marco's beak mid-air; Marco's beak is still frozen open in the shape of the fish, feathers flying in all directions.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same shot: Nia already climbing away with the trout, a single turquoise feather drifting down, Marco staring at his empty beak.

scenes.narration: Marco chased her across the river, wingtips skimming the water.
scenes.image_prompt: Marco skimming inches above the river at full speed, wingtips cutting twin white wakes, Nia a little ahead above the far trees, the sunset smeared into gold streaks.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same shot closer: Marco's beak almost touching her tail feathers, the wake behind him spraying upward.

scenes.narration: She landed on a dead branch, and did not eat.
scenes.image_prompt: Nia perched on a bare dead branch holding the trout in her beak untouched, staring down not at Marco but at something below; Marco landing behind her, mid-flap, confusion on his face.

scenes.narration: Beneath her, a nest. Empty, except for one pale egg.
scenes.image_prompt: Looking down into a small twig nest in the roots below the dead branch holding one lone pale speckled egg; Nia's shadow falls across it; warm evening light makes the egg glow faintly.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same nest, the camera slightly closer: a single drop of water falls from the trout onto the egg's shell.

scenes.narration: Marco looked at the trout. He looked at the egg.
scenes.image_prompt: Close-up of Marco's amber eye reflecting both the silver trout and the glowing egg, a single tear-like drop of river water on his beak.

scenes.narration: He laid the trout beside the egg. Said nothing. Flew home.
scenes.image_prompt: Marco gently placing the huge silver trout in the nest beside the glowing egg, Nia watching with her beak open in shock, a warm halo of light around the three.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same moment: Marco already lifting away, wings beating, Nia still frozen, the trout shining beside the egg.

scenes.narration: Marco nodded. The branch was no longer his.
scenes.image_prompt: Marco turning slowly away from the river, head lowered, long shadow stretching behind him across the old branch, the faded blue feather still caught in the bark.

scenes.narration: But the river had one more rule.
scenes.delivery: a beat of hush, then lifted
scenes.image_prompt: The turtle's eye opening slightly wider, the faintest hint of a smile on his shell-hard face, as the frog on the lily pad slowly rotates its head toward him.

scenes.narration: The branch belongs to whoever gives away the perfect fish.
scenes.image_prompt: Nia gently landing on Marco's worn branch while Marco stands beside her, both small and stunned beneath the huge turtle, the sky turning violet.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same scene: Marco and Nia now sharing the branch, shoulder to shoulder, the turtle looking pleased.

scenes.narration: Humans live by this river too.
scenes.image_prompt: Dissolve into a dim empty open-plan office at dusk: Sam sits alone at a desk under one lamp, one finished report in front of him, shoulders slumped, eyes on a wall clock reading 6:58; city lights beyond the window.

scenes.narration: One report. One deadline. And Jo, drowning two desks away.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide office view: Sam in the foreground holding his finished report against his chest; two desks behind him Jo buries her face in her hands behind a collapsing tower of unfinished papers, a cold mug tipped on its side.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same view: Sam's head has turned toward Jo, eyebrows raised; Jo's tower of papers has slid one more layer, a single page floating to the floor.

scenes.narration: Sam looked at his report. He looked at Jo. He walked over.
scenes.image_prompt: Close two-shot: Sam gently sets his finished report on Jo's desk, his hand still on the corner and his face quietly pained; Jo looks up in disbelief, eyes wide and wet.

scenes.narration: Next morning, the boss asked who had saved the project.
scenes.image_prompt: Bright morning office: the boss stands between the desks holding Jo's report with a big smile; Jo points past the boss straight at Sam, who sits at the back with an astonished blank face and a coffee halfway to his mouth.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Same office a beat later: the boss is walking toward Sam with an outstretched hand and a huge grin; Sam's coffee has dropped to the desk, spilling.

scenes.narration: At dusk, the egg began to hum.
scenes.image_prompt: Close on the nest in near darkness; the pale egg now glowing steadily, a ring of faint ripples spreading across the water around it; the frog sits at the edge of frame fully illuminated by the egg's light.

scenes.narration: The turtle, who had not moved all day, was on the far bank.
scenes.image_prompt: Wide dusk shot: the huge turtle sitting calmly on the far bank in deep blue light exactly where nothing was before; on the flat rock where he was is still a perfect wet turtle-shaped patch; the frog watching.

scenes.narration: Nobody asked how. The river keeps accounts. This is tidalfolio.
scenes.image_prompt: The frog sitting on the lily pad, wearing the enormous brown leather boot, staring directly into the camera with a blank face; behind it the glowing egg rests quietly in the nest.

youtube.title: He Had Until Sunset To Catch One Fish (Bird Banter #1)
youtube.description: A kingfisher, a debt to the river, a rival who wants his branch, and one egg that hums at dusk. Sometimes the only way to keep what you love is to let it go. Part 2 is coming. Subscribe for more wild moments.
youtube.pinned_comment: Would you have given the fish away? Be honest. And who was the egg?

tiktok.caption: He gave up the perfect fish. Then the egg started humming. Part 2 soon. #BirdBanter
